title: WPMS/1469/2016 of Food Corporation Of India Vs Food Corporation Of India AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Recall Application No. 1385 of 2018
Delay in Recall Appl. No. 16836 of 2018
In
Writ Petition No. 1469 of 2016 (M/S)
Food Corporation of India ÖÖ Petitioner
Vs.
Food Corporation of India Shramik Sangh and others
 ÖÖRespondents

Mr. V.K. Kohli, Senior Advocate with Mr. Bhuvnesh Joshi,
Advocate for the petitioner / review applicant.
Mr. M.C. Pant, Advocate for the respondent / opposite party.
Honíble Lok Pal Singh, J.
Heard learned counsel for the parties on recall
application being MCC No. 1385 of 2018.
2. Brief facts of the case are that petitioner-Food
Corporation of India had challenged the judgment and
award dated 29.02.2016, passed by the Presiding Officer,
Central Government Industrial Tribunal-cum-Labour Court
in Industrial Dispute No. 192 of 2011, titled as, General
Secretary, Food Corporation of India, Shramik Sangh vs.
Regional Manager, Food Corporation of India.
3. Learned co-ordinate Bench of this Court, vide
judgment and order dated 28.10.2016, dismissed the writ
petition and saddled a cost of Rs. 25,000/- on the
petitioner.
4. Feeling aggrieved, petitioner preferred a review
application, being MCC No. 853 of 2016, but same was
dismissed by order dated 19.12.2016 with the observation
that there is no merit in the review application.
5. Still feeling aggrieved, petitioner preferred SLP(C) No.
9778 of 2017 before the Honíble Supreme Court. The same

2
was also dismissed vide judgment and order dated
03.04.2017.
6. On dismissal of SLP, order dated 28.10.2016, passed
by this Court dismissing the writ petition and order dated
19.12.2016, passed on review application were affirmed.
Thereafter, respondent filed modification application being
MCC No. 626 of 2018 with the following prayer:-
ìthat petitioner be directed to comply the
judgment of the CGIT in its letter and spirit
within a specific time as prescribed by this
Honíble Court without asking the extraneous
documents which are having no significance in
view of the judgment of CGIT and to
modify/clarify the judgment dated 28.10.2016
accordingly and/or to pass any such other
further order which this Honíble Court may
deem fit and proper in the present facts and
circumstances of the case.
7. Thereafter, the co-ordinate Bench after hearing the
learned counsel for the parties passed an order dated
01.06.2018 on the modification application moved by the
respondent. The same is extracted hereunder:
ìNo ground has been made out for
modification of the order, except that the
respondent-Corporation is directed to implement
the award, as it is, without seeking any further
details from the workmen.
Accordingly, the modification application is
allowed to the above extentî.

8. Recall application has been filed to recall the order
dated 01.06.2018, being passed by the co-ordinate
Bench, along with delay condonation application. There
is delay of 102 days in filing the recall application.
Despite time granted to the opposite party, objection to
the delay condonation application has not been filed.

3
9. Delay of 102 days in filing the recall application is
ordinate and has sufficiently been explained and the
averments are supported by an affidavit. Thus, the delay
condonation application is allowed. Delay of 102 days in
filing the recall application is condoned.
10. Recall application has been filed to recall the order
dated 01.06.2018 on the ground that since, writ petition
was dismissed, review application filed by the petitioner
was dismissed and SLP preferred by the petitioner was
too dismissed, thereafter, modification application filed
by the respondent was not maintainable and same was
liable to be dismissed. It is contended that while hearing
the modification application, the co-ordinate Bench of
this Court has recorded the finding that no ground has
been made out for modification of the order, however, the
co-ordinate Bench has issued directions to the petitioner
to implement the award, as it is, without seeking further
details from the workmen and allowed the modification
application.
11. Learned counsel for the petitioner / review
applicant would submit that since it has been observed
in the order dated 01.06.2018 that no ground has been
made out to modify the order, the application was ought
to be rejected. He would further submit that after
dismissal of the case the Court becomes functus officio.
Further, it is submitted that arithmetical or clerical
mistake can be corrected by way of modification but the
basic structure of the judgment cannot be changed by
issuing further directions in the guise of modification.

4
12. Learned counsel for the review applicant has placed
reliance upon the judgment of Honíble Apex Court in the
case of BHEL and others vs. Amit Kumar reported in
(2007) 1SCC 610 and would submit that since the writ
petition was dismissed. Thereafter review application
and the SLP were dismissed. Thus, there was no
occasion to issue directions to the petitioner Corporation
in the guise of modification of the order.
13. By means of modification application, the Court can
correct/modify the order to the extent of arithmetical or
clerical mistake, in view of the provision contained in
section 152 CPC. For kind reference, section 152 of
C.P.C. is extracted hereunder:-
ì152. Amendment of judgments, decrees or orders:-
Clerical or arithmetical mistakes in judgments, decrees
or orders or errors arising therein from any accidental
slip or omission may at any time be corrected by the
Court either of its own motion or on the application of
any of the parties.î
14. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent /
opposite party would submit that since the order has
been affirmed upto the Honíble Apex Court, therefore, the
petitioner Corporation is bound to execute the award as
it is. He would further submit that the learned Judge did
not commit any illegality in allowing the modification
application directing the petitioner Corporation to
implement the award.
15. Submission advanced by the learned counsel for the
respondent / opposite party is misconceived. Once the
writ petition was dismissed, this Court could not

5
substitute its observations in regard to the execution of
the award. It is the Labour Court only, who can execute
the award. Thus, I have no hesitation to say that the
learned Judge has committed illegality in allowing the
modification application by order dated 01.06.2018 and
has exceeded in its jurisdiction, allowing the modification
application.
16. I find force in the contention of the learned counsel
for the petitioner / review applicant that after dismissal
of the writ petition, review application and SLP, the Court
becomes functus officio and the modification application
ought not to be entertained to issue directions to the
petitioner Corporation to implement the Award, as it is,
without seeking any further details from the workmen.
17. It is apt to note that the writ petition was earlier
dismissed on 28.10.2016. Review application and SLP too
were dismissed. Thereafter, on a modification application
moved by the respondent, order dated 01.06.2018 was
passed directing the petitioner Corporation to implement
the Award. It is the Labour Court, who has to implement
the Award on an execution application. This Court
cannot convert itself into an Executing Court and to
issue any direction to the Corporation to implement the
Award. Such direction issued by the co-ordinate Bench
of this Court vide order dated 01.06.2018 is absolutely
without jurisdiction.
18. For the forgoing reasons, I am of the view that
learned Judge has exceeded its jurisdiction upon hearing
the modification application to make observations and
directing the Corporation to implement the Award, as it

6
is, without seeking any further details from the workmen.
Such direction issued by the co-ordinate bench of this
Court on a modification application is absolutely without
jurisdiction. Thus the order dated 01.06.2018 being
without jurisdiction is liable to be recalled. The same is
hereby recalled.
19. Consequently, recall application is allowed.
Modification application MCC no. 626 of 2018 stands
rejected.
20. No order as to costs.
 (Lok Pal Singh, J.)
Parul 25.03.2019
